newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds open strong after durable goods data.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds open strong after durable goods data.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened stronger on Thursday, pulled up by U.S. Treasuries after the release of weaker-than-expected U.S. economic data, dealers said.

"We're finally starting to see more signs of slowing than growth in the U.S.. We may be at a juncture in that the U.S. may start to moderate," said Will Sutherland, vice-president of fixed income with Altamira Investment Services.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.35 at C$103.30 to yield 7.705 percent against the U.S. 30-year benchmark which rose 16/32 to yield 6.89 percent.
The spread between the two benchmark bonds widened to 82 basis points from 81 points at the close on Wednesday.

Both Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets rallied after the U.S. Commerce department reported that August durable goods fell by a greater-than-expected 3.1 percent. The market was also buoyed by higher-than-expected U.S. jobless claims data.
In new issue news, the province of Saskatchewan on Thursday set a C$200 million, 6.125 percent bond due, October 10, 2001, said lead manager CIBC Wood Gundy Securities Inc.
The issue was priced at C$99.025 to yield 6.356 percent with a spread of 10 basis points over the Government of Canada 7.0 percent bond due September, 2001.
The new issue will be delivered on October 10.
In other prices, the 7.0 percent of 2006 rose C$0.22 to C$98.98 to yield 7.141 percent. The U.S. 10-year benchmark rose 7/32 to yield 6.66 percent.
The spread between the two benchmark bonds was 48 basis points, unchanged from Wednesday's close.
The three-month cash bill traded at 3.85 percent against the U.S. three-month bill at 5.02 percent.
